cancer_indication: Approved for node-positive breast cancer (after doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide) and for metastatic breast cancer post-anthracycline; standard (neo)adjuvant agent for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and used in HER2+ disease in combination with trastuzumab.
moa: Paclitaxel binds β-tubulin in microtubules, stabilizing them against depolymerization and blocking the dynamic reorganization required for mitosis, causing G2/M arrest and abnormal multipolar spindle formation. Mitotic blockade triggers apoptosis, partly via interference with the anti-apoptotic protein BCL2, which paclitaxel can bind and inactivate. Paclitaxel can also activate innate immune and interferon programs in tumor cells and can agonize TLR4 signaling, although TLR4 signaling in cancer cells tends to promote survival and resistance.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Gene program controlling the G2→M transition and mitotic checkpoint functions, reflecting regulation of mitosis and G2/M transition.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: Cell-cycle checkpoint activity is central to breast-tumor proliferation and treatment response, especially in rapidly dividing tumors where mitotic control is a key vulnerability.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Very high baseline G2/M may coexist with robust spindle checkpoints and CIN-tolerant programs in some HR+/HER2– or TNBC tumors, allowing survival despite taxane-induced spindle stress.
Swanton et al., “Regulators of mitotic arrest and taxane resistance in breast cancer.” Cancer Cell 2007. PMID: 17560332; Swanton, “CIN and taxane response.” Nat Rev Cancer 2009. PMID: 19458043.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High G2/M in Luminal B and basal-like/TNBC means many cells enter mitosis, the phase where paclitaxel-stabilized microtubules block spindle function and trigger mitotic arrest.
Jordan & Wilson, “Microtubules as a target for anticancer drugs.” Nat Rev Cancer 2004. PMID: 15057285; Nakayama et al., CDK1/2 activity predicts paclitaxel benefit in breast cancer. PMID: 19239702.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low baseline G2/M indicates few mitotic targets, so paclitaxel’s microtubule-stabilizing MOA has little opportunity to induce lethal spindle damage at treatment start.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285; Awosika et al., “Paclitaxel.” StatPearls 2023.(NCBI)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (for breast baseline): With very low G2/M, there are too few dividing cells for a mitotic spindle poison to be globally effective; sensitivity would require a later proliferative burst, not a true baseline predictor.
Mechanistic logic based on paclitaxel’s requirement for mitotic entry; DrugBank Paclitaxel DB01229.(DrugBank)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent high G2/M after treatment can reflect reversible mitotic arrest with activated checkpoints that allow repair, slippage, and emergence of resistant clones rather than apoptotic death.
Swanton 2007. PMID: 17560332; Castle et al., “Mechanisms of kinetic stabilization by paclitaxel.” Mol Biol Cell 2017. PMID: 28331005.(Molecular Biology of the Cell)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In sensitive tumors, paclitaxel causes accumulation in G2/M with multipolar spindles and chromosome missegregation; transiently increased G2/M signature marks lethal mitotic arrest.
Zasadil et al., “Chromosome missegregation by paclitaxel.” Sci Transl Med 2014. PMID: 24670687; Xiao et al., “Taxol stabilizes microtubules and reduces dynamics.” PNAS 2006. PMID: 17028153.(PNAS)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: G2/M down-regulation with residual tumor suggests escape into quiescence/senescence; rare but possible route to functional resistance to further mitotic targeting.
Reviews of taxane resistance and dormant cancer cells in breast cancer (Abouzeid 2025 paclitaxel resistance review).(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: After effective paclitaxel killing, most dividing cells are eliminated, so bulk G2/M expression drops as a pharmacodynamic marker of response.
Zasadil 2014. PMID: 24670687; Abouzeid 2025, “Paclitaxel resistance in breast cancer – current challenges.”(ScienceDirect)

HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE.description: Gene program related to mitotic spindle structure/function and microtubule dynamics required for mitosis.
HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE.interpretation: Mitotic spindle integrity is required for successful cell division; reliance on mitotic machinery is a hallmark of proliferative breast cancers.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Strong spindle gene upregulation with intact checkpoints and survival signaling can produce highly proliferative yet taxane-tolerant clones in some TNBCs.
Swanton 2009. PMID: 19458043; Abouzeid 2025 review on paclitaxel-resistant TNBC.(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High mitotic spindle activity in Luminal B and basal-like tumors means strong dependence on dynamic microtubules, which paclitaxel stabilizes to disrupt anaphase and trigger death.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285; Foland et al., paclitaxel-induced mitotic block. J Cell Sci 2005. PMID: 16236763.(PMC)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low spindle gene expression implies fewer cells relying on mitotic spindle dynamics, limiting the cytotoxic advantage of spindle stabilization.
Mechanistic extrapolation from paclitaxel targeting β-tubulin and mitotic spindles(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (as baseline predictor): Without substantial spindle activity, paclitaxel has little direct target; baseline low spindle cannot mechanistically predict high sensitivity in breast tumors.
Logic from MOA; paclitaxel requires dynamic spindle microtubules for maximal effect.(NCBI)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Sustained spindle gene expression after paclitaxel may reflect selection for clones that maintain functional spindles via altered tubulin isotypes or checkpoint rewiring.
Yang, “Taxol®: the first microtubule stabilizing agent.” IJMS 2017. PMID: 28757572.(MDPI)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Short-term increase in mitotic spindle signatures reflects pharmacologic mitotic arrest, preceding apoptosis in sensitive HR+/HER2– and TNBC tumors.
Zasadil 2014. PMID: 24670687; Foland 2005. PMID: 16236763.(PMC)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Strong downregulation with persistent disease can indicate transition to non-cycling, EMT-like or stem-like states that evade spindle targeting.
Abouzeid 2025 paclitaxel resistance review in breast cancer.(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Clearance of mitotically active cells after paclitaxel decreases spindle gene expression, marking effective tumor cell kill.
StatPearls Paclitaxel(NCBI); DrugBank DB01229(DrugBank)

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Programmed cell death pathway activity, including regulation by anti-apoptotic factors such as BCL2.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Apoptotic competence influences whether breast tumor cells undergo cell death under cytotoxic stress and is a major determinant of chemotherapy responsiveness.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: In some Luminal A/B tumors, high apoptosis signatures may reflect compensatory BCL-2/MCL-1 overexpression that buffers paclitaxel-induced damage.
Ruvolo, “Bcl-2 regulation of apoptosis.” Leukemia 2001. PMID: 11238947.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: TNBC and HER2+ tumors with strong pro-apoptotic priming (e.g., high BAX/BAK, low BCL-2) more readily execute mitochondrial apoptosis when mitotic arrest is triggered by paclitaxel.
Miller et al., BAK-dependent paclitaxel apoptosis. PLoS One 2013. PMID: 23593244.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Apoptosis-low HR+/HER2– tumors with high BCL-2 or MCL-1 are classic examples of taxane resistance because survival signaling dominates after spindle damage.
Kaboli et al., “Chemoresistance in breast cancer and survival pathways.” Front Oncol 2020. PMCID: PMC8569340.(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (as a clean predictor): Without basal apoptotic competence, paclitaxel-triggered mitotic stress cannot reliably translate into caspase activation; sensitivity would need other lethal pathways (e.g., necrosis) not captured by this hallmark.
Conceptual extrapolation from mitochondrial apoptosis requirement in taxane cytotoxicity.(PMC)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors may show a transient rise in apoptotic transcripts but survive via rapid upregulation of anti-apoptotic proteins and DNA repair, leading to incomplete cell death and eventual resistance.
Song et al., BCL-2 phosphorylation network. Br J Pharmacol 2019. PMID: 31001901.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In sensitive breast tumors, paclitaxel-induced mitotic arrest drives BCL-2 loop-domain phosphorylation, cytochrome c release and caspase activation, producing robust upregulation of apoptosis pathways.
Srivastava et al., “Bcl-2 loop and paclitaxel-induced apoptosis.” PNAS 1999. PMID: 10097135.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Surviving cells can dampen apoptotic signaling via upregulating BCL-2/MCL-1 or activating PI3K/AKT, resulting in reduced apoptosis gene expression and clinical resistance.
Kaboli 2020. PMCID: PMC8569340(ScienceDirect); Miricescu 2020 PI3K/AKT in breast cancer.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In gBRCA1/2 or HRD+ tumors, massive early apoptosis may remove most tumor cells so that later bulk samples show low apoptotic transcription simply because few viable cells remain.
Cross-cancer DNA damage/apoptosis logic, consistent with high chemosensitivity of BRCA-mutated breast cancers to DNA-damaging/mitotic agents.

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.description: Innate immune/interferon-stimulated gene programs induced in tumor cells, reflecting interferon pathway activation.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.interpretation: Interferon-associated transcriptional programs can shape anti-tumor immunity and tumor–immune interactions in breast cancer, particularly in immune-infiltrated disease contexts.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Chronic IFN-γ signaling can induce PD-L1 and immunosuppressive programs that attenuate chemotherapy-only benefit in some ER– tumors (mechanism mostly inferred from immune checkpoint literature).
Weichselbaum et al., IFN-related DNA damage resistance signature. Nat Med 2008. PMCID: PMC2587578.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: TNBC and HER2+ tumors with IFN-γ-high, T-cell–inflamed microenvironments are more likely to respond to taxane-based chemotherapy and chemo-immunotherapy.
Opdam et al., immune gene sets predicting taxane benefit. Clin Cancer Res 2024.(PMC)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: IFN-γ–low, immune-cold HR+/HER2– or TNBC tumors have limited cytotoxic T-cell support and generally respond worse to paclitaxel-containing regimens.
Early breast cancer neoadjuvant immune-markers: GeparSepto (NCT01583426) immune activity vs taxane response.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Highly proliferative Luminal B tumors can still be paclitaxel-sensitive despite low IFN-γ when mitotic rate, not immunity, dominates treatment response.
Reinisch et al., dose-dense taxane-based adjuvant therapy by subtype.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Paclitaxel-induced IFN-γ can drive PD-L1 and adaptive immune resistance, limiting long-term control if not combined with checkpoint blockade.
PD-1/PD-L1 reviews in breast cancer; Jin et al., “PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in breast cancer.” Mol Cancer 2024.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Metronomic paclitaxel in TNBC models increases T-cell infiltration and IFN-γ signaling, enhancing response to PD-1 antibodies and indicating chemo-induced IFN-γ can mark sensitivity.
Chen et al., metronomic paclitaxel + PD-1 in TNBC. Am J Transl Res 2020. PMCID: PMC7061845.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to induce or maintain IFN-γ programs after therapy suggests persistent immune exclusion, which correlates with poor chemo-immunotherapy response in TNBC.
Longitudinal immune-gene monitoring in TNBC chemo-ICI trials (e.g., KEYNOTE-522 subgroup analyses).
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In complete responders, IFN-γ signatures can decline over time as tumor burden falls and inflammatory stimulus disappears, despite an initially favorable immune response.
Conceptual based on serial biopsies in early TNBC regimens showing immune normalization after pCR.

REACTOME_NFKB_AND_MAP_KINASES_ACTIVATION.description: TLR4-linked signaling that activates NF-κB and MAPK pathways and can promote inflammatory cytokine production (e.g., IL-6/IL-8).
REACTOME_NFKB_AND_MAP_KINASES_ACTIVATION.interpretation: Inflammatory survival signaling in breast tumor cells can influence progression, metastasis, and treatment outcomes through cytokine-driven feedback and stress-response programs.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: TLR4/NF-κB/MAPK-high TNBC cells express IL-6/IL-8 and anti-apoptotic genes, showing poor paclitaxel response because NF-κB-driven survival programs counteract mitotic death.
Rajput et al., “TLR4 is a novel determinant of the response to paclitaxel in breast cancer.” Mol Cancer Ther 2013. PMID: 23720768.(PubMed)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: If TLR4 expression is mainly on APCs rather than tumor cells, NF-κB/MAPK activation can support antitumor immunity and augment taxane benefit (shown mostly in murine models, cross-cancer extrapolation).
Immunogenic chemotherapy reviews; Galluzzi et al., Cell Death Differ 2012.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Very low TLR4/NF-κB signaling in myeloid cells may blunt innate sensing of dying tumor cells, reducing immunogenic contribution to paclitaxel efficacy.
Galluzzi et al., immunogenic cell death and DAMP signaling.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: TLR4-low breast tumors avoid paclitaxel-induced NF-κB survival activation and are more likely to undergo straightforward mitotic catastrophe.
Rajput 2013. PMID: 23720768(PubMed); Sootichote et al., TLR4 inhibition sensitizes to paclitaxel (ovarian, cross-cancer but mechanistically relevant).(SpringerLink)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Paclitaxel directly activates TLR4 in breast cancer cells, triggering NF-κB/MAPK and upregulating pro-survival cytokines, promoting chemoresistance and metastasis.
Rajput 2013. PMID: 23720768(PubMed); Volk-Draper et al., “Paclitaxel therapy promotes breast cancer metastasis via TLR4.” Cancer Res 2014. PMCID: PMC4185415.(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In immunologically hot tumors, NF-κB activation in innate immune cells could contribute to antitumor cytokine cascades that synergize with paclitaxel.
Immunomodulatory metronomic chemotherapy review (Jan 2024).(ScienceDirect)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Excessive pharmacological NF-κB suppression in immune cells might blunt antigen presentation and limit durable benefit, even if tumor-intrinsic resistance is unchanged.
Metronomic chemo & immune reprogramming reviews in breast cancer(PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In TLR4+ tumors, blocking or down-modulating NF-κB/MAPK after paclitaxel restores apoptotic response and prevents cytokine-mediated repair.
Sootichote et al., Compound A attenuates TLR4-mediated paclitaxel resistance. BMC Cancer 2018. PMID: 29661103.(SpringerLink)

REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING.description: PI3K/AKT survival signaling that promotes cell survival and can protect cells from apoptosis.
REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT signaling is a major pro-survival axis in breast cancer that supports growth and cell survival under therapeutic stress.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K/AKT activation (PIK3CA mutations/PTEN loss) upregulates BCL-2/MCL-1 and survival signaling, conferring broad chemoresistance including to paclitaxel in HR+/HER2– and TNBC.
Kaboli et al., PI3K/AKT and chemoresistance in breast cancer. Front Oncol 2020. PMCID: PMC8569340.(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2+ and Luminal B tumors with PI3K/AKT upregulation remain paclitaxel-sensitive because high proliferation outweighs survival signaling under intense mitotic stress.
Miricescu et al., PI3K/AKT in breast cancer. Int J Mol Sci 2020.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: PI3K/AKT-low tumors can still be resistant if alternative pathways (e.g., TLR4/NF-κB, ABCB1) dominate, but PI3K/AKT downregulation itself does not induce resistance.
Dong et al., PI3K/AKT and multidrug resistance (cross-cancer). Front Pharmacol 2021. PMCID: PMC7886139.(Spandidos Publications)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Reduced PI3K/AKT signaling lowers anti-apoptotic buffering, so paclitaxel-induced damage triggers stronger mitochondrial apoptosis in such breast tumors.
Kaboli 2020. PMCID: PMC8569340.(ScienceDirect)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Paclitaxel stress can activate RTKs and cytokine receptors, driving rebound PI3K/AKT that supports survival and cancer stem-like cells, leading to acquired taxane resistance.
Dong 2021. PMCID: PMC7886139(Spandidos Publications); Abouzeid 2025.(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: AKT up-ticks may be transient and overridden by stronger pro-apoptotic signaling, so overall phenotype remains sensitive despite temporary PI3K/AKT activation.
Miller 2013 BAK-dependent paclitaxel apoptosis. PMID: 23593244.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Profound AKT suppression could select for alternative resistance mechanisms (autophagy, NF-κB) but AKT downregulation alone is not a typical driver of paclitaxel resistance.
Dong 2021. PMCID: PMC7886139.(Spandidos Publications)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders, paclitaxel plus pathway crosstalk leads to decreased PI3K/AKT signaling, facilitating BAX/BAK activation and cell death.
Hu et al., PI3K inhibition reverses MDR and enhances paclitaxel in breast cancer. Cell Death Dis 2015. PMID: 26492368.

KEGG_CYTOKINE_CYTOKINE_RECEPTOR_INTERACT.description: Cytokine signaling network including IL-6/IL-8 and related cytokine–receptor interactions that can create autocrine signaling loops.
KEGG_CYTOKINE_CYTOKINE_RECEPTOR_INTERACT.interpretation: Cytokine signaling can modulate tumor–microenvironment interactions and tumor cell survival/progression programs in breast cancer.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: A cytokine milieu dominated by IL-6/IL-8/TNF-α promotes EMT, stemness and chemoresistance in TNBC, offsetting paclitaxel benefit.
Abd El-Aziz et al., ABCB1 and IL-6/IL-8 in TNBC resistance. PMCID: PMC7909869.(PMC); KEGG hsa04060.(PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Th1/IFN-γ/IL-12-rich cytokine signatures in immune-hot TNBC/HER2+ associate with better response to taxane-based chemo.
Opdam 2024 immune gene sets and taxane benefit.(PMC); KEGG hsa04060.(PMC)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low cytokine–receptor activity marks immune-cold microenvironments with poor effector recruitment and generally worse paclitaxel outcomes.
NCT01583426 (GeparSepto) immune analyses; metronomic chemo reviews in breast cancer.(MDPI)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Highly proliferative Luminal B tumors may still be taxane-sensitive even with low immune cytokine signatures, because cell-intrinsic mitotic vulnerability dominates.
Clinical anthracycline/taxane adjuvant trials by subtype (e.g., Lee et al., weekly paclitaxel in operable breast cancer).(AACR Journals)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Paclitaxel-induced IL-6/IL-8 and other cytokines via TLR4 promote myeloid recruitment, angiogenesis, and metastatic spread, driving resistance.
Volk-Draper 2014. PMCID: PMC4185415(Europe PMC); Rajput 2013. PMID: 23720768.(PubMed)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Metronomic paclitaxel reshapes cytokine networks to favor T-cell infiltration and synergize with PD-1 blockade in TNBC.
Liu 2025, “Metronomic Chemotherapy in Breast Cancer.” PMCID: PMC12602094.(PMC); Chen 2020 TNBC PD-1 + metronomic PTX. PMCID: PMC7061845.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Failure to induce beneficial cytokine signaling after therapy can indicate absence of immunogenic cell death, correlating with poor combined chemo-immune response.
Muraro/Bravetti 2023 reviews on metronomic chemo and immune modulation.(MDPI)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: After initial activation and tumor shrinkage, normalization of cytokine levels can reflect resolution of inflammation in responders.
Long-term follow-up in metronomic MBC cohorts (Cazzaniga 2022).(MDPI)

KEGG_ABC_TRANSPORTERS.description: ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux processes involving transporters such as ABCB1 and ABCC3 that export drugs from cells.
KEGG_ABC_TRANSPORTERS.interpretation: Drug efflux capacity affects intracellular exposure to chemotherapy and is a key determinant of treatment failure and refractory disease biology.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Overexpression of ABCB1/P-gp and ABCG2 in TNBC actively effluxes paclitaxel, reducing intracellular drug and causing multidrug resistance.
Abd El-Aziz et al., “Role of ABCB1 in mediating chemoresistance of TNBC.” Biosci Rep 2021. PMCID: PMC7909869.(PMC); Abouzeid 2025.(ScienceDirect); KEGG hsa02010.
Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (tumor-intrinsic): High functional ABC transporter activity in tumor cells, by definition, limits intracellular paclitaxel accumulation and cannot predict true sensitivity.
P-gp MDR reviews: Tian 2023. Int J Oncol 2023.(Spandidos Publications)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors with low ABC expression can still be resistant if non-efflux mechanisms (TLR4/NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, tubulin mutations) dominate; ABC-low status alone doesn’t guarantee response.
Abouzeid 2025 paclitaxel resistance review.(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: ABC-low HR+/HER2– and TNBC tumors retain more paclitaxel intracellularly, typically showing better cytotoxic responses.
Chang et al., ABCB1 polymorphisms and paclitaxel response. Ann Oncol 2009. PMID: 19182210.(Annals of Oncology)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Paclitaxel exposure selects for and induces ABCB1/ABCG2, further enhancing efflux and mediating acquired taxane resistance.
Tang et al., fast induction of P-gp-mediated drug resistance. Anticancer Res 2015.(IIAR Journals); Aldonza 2016. Oncotarget.(Oncotarget)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Early cycles may show partial ABC induction in dying cells, but global tumor sensitivity persists if efflux never reaches protective levels.
Sun et al., P-gp modulation reverses MDR (cross-cancer). Int J Mol Sci 2023.(MDPI)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: When resistance is driven by non-ABC mechanisms, ABC transcripts may decrease while cells remain taxane-resistant via altered tubulin and survival signaling.
Tian 2023 MDR review.(Spandidos Publications)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Pharmacologic inhibition or epigenetic downregulation of P-gp during treatment enhances intracellular paclitaxel and re-sensitizes MDR breast cancer cells.
Sun 2023 P-gp inhibitor EC31.(MDPI)

REACTOME_CELL_CYCLE.description: Overall cell-cycle gene expression programs controlling proliferation and progression through cell-cycle phases.
REACTOME_CELL_CYCLE.interpretation: Cell-cycle activity reflects proliferative state and underpins aggressiveness and chemotherapy responsiveness in breast cancers.

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: A subset of immune-cold, ultra-proliferative TNBCs relapse despite intense anthracycline–taxane therapy, indicating that high cell-cycle alone can coexist with resistance.
TNBC high-proliferation recurrence signatures (proteogenomic studies 2021–2023).
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Luminal B and basal-like tumors with high cell-cycle activity place many cells into G2/M, where paclitaxel exerts its cytotoxic effect.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285(MDPI); Lee et al., weekly paclitaxel improves pCR. J Clin Oncol 2005.(AACR Journals)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low cell-cycle (e.g., Luminal A) indicates indolent disease where the absolute gain from mitotic poisons like paclitaxel is modest.
Miricescu 2020 AKT/proliferation in breast cancer.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Genomically unstable but slow-cycling tumors may still be vulnerable when occasional divisions are catastrophically perturbed by paclitaxel.
Zasadil 2014 multipolar spindle kill. PMID: 24670687.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Surviving clones that recover from mitotic arrest re-enter the cell cycle with aggressive proliferation, contributing to relapse.
Abouzeid 2025.(ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Short-term cell-cycle gene elevation can mark arrested cells en route to apoptosis in sensitive tumors.
Samaan et al., paclitaxel’s cell-cycle effects in breast cancer (review).

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Surviving cells may adopt a quiescent phenotype that is inherently less sensitive to subsequent mitotic targeting.
Dormancy/therapy resistance reviews (PI3K/AKT/mTOR-mediated).(Spandidos Publications)
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Marked loss of cycling tumor cells after paclitaxel yields broad downregulation of cell-cycle programs in responders.
Samaan (2019) and StatPearls paclitaxel(NCBI)

HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.description: Angiogenesis-related gene programs associated with pro-angiogenic signals and blood-vessel formation.
HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.interpretation: Angiogenesis supports tumor growth and progression and can be influenced by inflammatory cytokine signaling in breast cancer.

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong VEGF/angiogenesis signaling sustains vascular support and often correlates with aggressive, chemoresistant breast disease.
Bocci, “Pharmacological bases of paclitaxel antiangiogenic activity.” Angiogenesis 2013. PMID: 23891595.(SpringerLink)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Moderately angiogenic, well-perfused tumors may initially facilitate paclitaxel delivery, allowing short-term sensitivity despite pro-angiogenic signaling.
Vascular normalization concepts in chemo (multiple solid-tumor studies).

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Severely hypoxic, poorly vascularized tumors may be underexposed to paclitaxel, limiting efficacy despite low angiogenic gene expression.
Hypoxia and drug delivery reviews in solid tumors.
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Small, early lesions with modest angiogenesis can still be well-controlled by standard paclitaxel dosing.
Metastatic vs early breast cancer metronomic chemo outcomes.(MDPI)

Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Paclitaxel-TLR4–driven cytokines (e.g., IL-8) can stimulate endothelial cells and pro-angiogenic programs, favoring metastasis and resistance.
Volk-Draper 2014. PMCID: PMC4185415(Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Transient vascular normalization with functional angiogenesis may improve drug delivery and oxygenation, temporarily enhancing paclitaxel effect.
Bocci 2013 antiangiogenic review.(SpringerLink)

Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Excessive antiangiogenic pressure can select for hypoxia-adapted, invasive clones that later drive relapse despite initial vascular suppression.
Antiangiogenic therapy escape reviews.
Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low-dose metronomic paclitaxel reduces VEGF and increases thrombospondin-1, directly targeting tumor endothelium and contributing to durable responses in HR+/HER2– and TNBC MBC.
Tao et al., “Low-dose metronomic paclitaxel upregulates TSP-1 and is antiangiogenic in breast cancer.” Oncol Rep 2015. PMCID: PMC4278254.(PMC); Liu 2025 metronomic breast cancer review.(PMC)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Strong apoptotic signaling with intact p53 was described as favoring paclitaxel sensitivity, consistent with paclitaxel-induced mitotic arrest leading to programmed cell death.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Inhibition/knockdown of TLR4 was described as enhancing paclitaxel response by downregulating NF-κB/IL-6–mediated survival genes.
Downregulation of ABC transporters (including ABCB1/P-gp) was described as increasing intracellular paclitaxel retention, supporting improved response.
Downregulation of ABC transporters (including ABCC3) was described as increasing intracellular paclitaxel retention, supporting improved response.
Low BCL2 (and loss of anti-apoptotic BCL2) was described as favoring sensitivity by permitting apoptosis under paclitaxel-induced mitotic stress.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Overexpression/activation of TLR4 and downstream NF-κB/MAPK signaling was described as conferring a pro-survival inflammatory state and chemoresistance (including IL-6/IL-8 loops).
Elevated ABCB1/P-gp was described as exporting paclitaxel and lowering intracellular drug levels, contributing to resistance.
Elevated ABCC3 (including references to MRP3-mediated efflux) was described as exporting paclitaxel and lowering intracellular drug levels, contributing to resistance.
Paclitaxel-triggered IL-6 secretion via TLR4/NF-κB was described as contributing to autocrine survival/angiogenic feedback and chemoresistance.
Paclitaxel-triggered IL-8 secretion via TLR4/NF-κB was described as contributing to autocrine survival/angiogenic feedback and chemoresistance.
Upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2 was described as associated with greater chemoresistance in clinical practice context.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Downregulation of apoptotic machinery (including BAX) was described as blunting paclitaxel’s effect and contributing to resistance.
Downregulation/loss of tumor suppressors (p53/TP53) was described as blunting paclitaxel’s effect and contributing to resistance.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR⁺/HER2⁻ (Luminal A/B): Endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors are first-line for metastatic HR⁺ breast cancer. Paclitaxel is generally reserved for endocrine-refractory cases or high-risk adjuvant settings. Luminal A cancers (slow-growing, hormone-dependent) often derive minimal benefit from paclitaxel. Luminal B tumors (more proliferative) may respond better, but overall HR⁺ status is not predictive of taxane sensitivity.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2⁺: Paclitaxel is a backbone for HER2⁺ disease, used with trastuzumab (and pertuzumab) in (neo)adjuvant and first-line metastatic therapy. In HER2⁺ cancers not amenable to anthracyclines, trastuzumab+paclitaxel is standard. Paclitaxel’s role is mainly as part of HER2-targeted regimens; monotherapy paclitaxel is used in later-line metastatic settings when targeted options are exhausted.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.TNBC (Basal-like): Lack of ER/HER2 makes chemotherapy the mainstay. Single-agent paclitaxel (or nab-paclitaxel) is often used in neoadjuvant and metastatic TNBC. Approximately 20–30% of TNBC patients achieve pathological complete response with taxane-based neoadjuvant chemo. Trials (e.g. GeparOLA) are exploring paclitaxel combinations (with PARP inhibitors or immunotherapy) in HRD/TNBC subsets.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.gBRCA1/2 and HRD: Germline BRCA-mutant tumors (often TNBC or “Basal-like”) are generally sensitive to DNA-damaging agents (platinum) and show high pathologic response to neoadjuvant chemo. Paclitaxel does not specifically target DNA repair, so its sensitivity in BRCA-mutant/HRD tumors is similar to other TNBCs. Current guidelines prefer platinum or PARP inhibitors for BRCA-mutated BC, but paclitaxel remains an option in multiagent regimens.
